text: Riding a bike involves using both brakes and tires, with braking being the primary method for stopping. Brakes consist of various types, including rim brakes, disc brakes, and drum brakes, each with its own mechanism for applying force to the wheels and causing them to slow down. Tires, on the other hand, are responsible for absorbing the shock of the ride and providing the smooth and cushioned ride quality. Proper tire maintenance, such as checking air pressure, tire treads, and rim condition, is essential for optimal performance and safety while cycling. With these components working together, cyclists can enjoy the thrill and health benefits of this fun and accessible form of transportation.
